name: Mark Kelly
subject: Trump just called me pathetic on FOX News
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
#

While he was being interviewed on Fox News today, Trump found some time to come after me again.
[](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-mar26.Zy8qu0&refcode=em260313-1-90&t=1&akid=6392%2E6688874%2ErmrNg6)
Name calling doesn’t bother me.
What I find truly “pathetic” is a president who surrounds himself with yes men that never tell him he’s wrong. What bothers me is a draft dodging coward putting American troops in harm’s way from the comfort of his mansion.
Not everyone had a rich dad who could buy their way out of combat. Some of us answered our nation’s call and served proudly, and we understand the consequences of having a clueless commander in chief.
Mr. President, get off Fox News and into the Situation Room. This isn’t a game or one of your reality TV shows. This is real, lives are at stake, and families across the country are praying their loved ones come home safe from the war you just started.
They deserve to know why our country rushed into a war without a strategy or a goal.
I am demanding the White House and the President to answer that question. And I am going to continue doing anything I can to prevent this conflict from spiraling further out of control.
Hold fast, folks.
Don’t give up the ship.
Mark

Peter, I want to tell you something I don’t talk about much.
When you’re deployed to a combat zone, you get phone calls home. Not many. And they’re short. The connection is bad, the timing is worse, and you spend half the call pretending everything is fine so the people you love don’t worry.
**_My mom knew I wasn’t telling her the true situation._**
She knew that “I’m fine, mom” meant rockets had targeted the base that week. She knew that “it’s quiet here” meant I couldn’t tell her what was actually happening. And she knew that every time I said “I’ll be home soon,” there was a chance I wouldn’t be.
That’s the part of military service that doesn’t make the campaign ads.
We talk about the soldier. We don’t talk about the mom who can’t sleep. The dad who checks his phone every 30 minutes. The family who has to wonder if their loved ones will be home for Christmas this year.
My family lived that. For nine months while I was in Iraq, they carried the weight of not knowing if I’d make it home.
And they’re not special. They’re one of thousands of military families across this country who sacrifice in silence while politicians in Washington use the troops as props in photo ops and then forget they exist the second the cameras turn off.
I’m running for Congress because military families deserve more than a yellow ribbon magnet on someone’s bumper.
They deserve a representative who actually understands what it’s like. Who’s been on both sides of that phone call. Who knows that “supporting the troops” doesn’t mean clapping at an airport — it means fixing the VA, fighting for military spouse employment, making sure no veteran sleeps on a park bench, and making sure the men and women we send into harm’s way have a government that’s worthy of their sacrifice.
_**That’s what this campaign is about.**_
_**Not me. Not my Bronze Star. Not my resume.**_
_**The families.**_
Every mom who can’t sleep. Every kid who doesn’t understand why their parent is gone. Every veteran who comes home to a system that doesn’t care.
I’m fighting for them. And I’m asking you to fight with me. **Please, chip in whatever you can.**

**Republican Lawyers Hired to Block Eileen Laubacher from Democratic Caucus and Assembly**
_Laubacher Campaign Granted Motion to Intervene to Defend Caucus Process_
**Highlands Ranch, CO -** Democratic congressional candidate Trisha Calvarese has hired attorneys with deep ties to Donald Trump and the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC) to pursue a lawsuit attempting to prevent fellow Democrat Admiral Eileen Laubacher from participating in the Colorado Democratic caucus and assembly process.The Laubacher campaign filed a motion to intervene in the case to protect the integrity of the Democratic process and hold the Republican-connected lawyers accountable. Judge Bailey has granted the motion, allowing the campaign to participate in the proceedings.The attorneys now representing Calvarese, Christopher Murray and Julian Ellis of the First and Fourteenth law firm, have longstanding ties to Republican political operations. The firm currently represents the National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), which is tasked with protecting Lauren Boebert’s seat in Congress, and has also represented the Republican National Committee and the Colorado Republican Party. Murray and Ellis have worked directly for Donald Trump, including his efforts to resist congressional subpoenas related to the January 6th attack on the U.S. Capitol.**The campaign has issued the following statement:**
_“It’s deeply troubling that a Democratic congressional candidate would take money from Democratic donors to first hire an election-denying attorney—currently on probation for filing frivolous lawsuits against Democratic officials—to sue Colorado’s Democratic Party, and then add more lawyers to the case from the state’s top Republican law firm whose lawyers are on the payroll of the National Republican Congressional Committee and work for MAGA causes and candidates. This is a blatant attempt to damage Eileen Laubacher because Republicans know she’s the strongest Democrat to defeat Lauren Boebert._
_Trisha Calvarese has already lost this district twice, and this conduct shows she’s prepared to lose it again by joining forces with Donald Trump’s and the RNC’s lawyers to file a frivolous lawsuit. This race is too important. Democrats need to nominate a serious candidate to beat Boebert—and Admiral Laubacher is that candidate.”_ ##

eyes on November instead of scrambling to hit the next fundraising
deadline.

It means I spend less time chasing checks and more time talking to voters

Abdul

name: Dan Freeman
subject: We’re suing the Trump administration:
body:
The American people have a right to know whether the Trump administration plans to interfere with the midterm elections.
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?amount=20&refcode=em_20260313_6370_fr&refcode2=6370_22930333_JjmBEJ&akid=6370%2E22930333%2EJjmBEJ)
---
Derek,
This week, the DNC filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration under the Freedom of Information Act.
**We’re demanding transparency: If the Trump administration plans to interfere with November’s midterm elections, the American people have a right to know.**
In October, we sent 11 requests for information to the Justice Department, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Defense Department. Congress set a deadline for agencies to respond to information requests, and that deadline passed months ago. We’re done waiting.
President Trump has consistently attacked the integrity of American elections, in the courts and on the ground. The public has a right to know the administration’s plans for November.
We all remember President Trump asking Georgia’s secretary of state to “find 11,780 votes” after he lost by exactly that margin in 2020. More recently, President Trump told the _New York Times_ that he regretted not ordering the National Guard to seize voting machines in swing states he lost in the 2020 election. He’s even threatened to “nationalize” elections.
**The fact is, if the federal government is planning to deploy armed agents to the polls, we have a right to know. If they’re planning on sending troops, we have a right to know.**
That’s why we’re suing, Derek: to uncover any plans that the Trump Administration has failed to turn over, so the DNC can prepare for the fight ahead.
[**So if taking the Trump administration to court to force them to comply with the law is important to you, please consider chipping in $7 to the DNC today to help us continue our legal work and holding Trump accountable →**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-march-2026?refcode=em_20260313_6370_fr&amount=7&refcode2=6370_22930333_JjmBEJ&akid=6370%2E22930333%2EJjmBEJ)

In this edition, I will discuss what I have been up to at the Capitol, upcoming Xcel outages, how my bills are going, upcoming constituent events, happenings in the district and Rep. Pettersen’s summer internship program, and the news.

# [UPCOMING XCEL OUTAGES]()
---
|
---
| | Xcel Energy is closely monitoring and preparing for severe weather to start Saturday, March 14, beginning around midday, in Boulder and Jefferson counties. The National Weather Service has issued a Fire Weather Watch for this weather event.
To reduce the risk of wildfire and support public safety, Xcel Energy is planning for a possible Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) beginning on Saturday, March 14, beginning around 2 p.m., potentially impacting about 43,000 customers in Boulder and Jefferson counties, where the most severe conditions are forecasted.
Weather conditions are expected to start improving around 5 p.m. on March 14, though high winds that may create wildfire risk and cause outages are expected to continue through the weekend.
Please note, due to anticipated high winds, outages could take place outside of areas impacted by a PSPS, impacting restoration times.
The impacted areas and number of customers affected may continue to change as weather conditions evolve and Xcel teams refine the scope of the PSPS event. Their goal is to limit the impact of a PSPS event as much as possible while effectively managing high wildfire risk.
It is possible that customers impacted by weather-related outages on Thursday, March 12, may experience additional disruption due to either a possible PSPS or high winds on Saturday, March 14.
Customers in Boulder and Jefferson counties can look up their address on the Xcel Energy statewide [outage map](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=01488bb65e&e=8249791cac), which displays the number of customers experiencing outages and anticipated restoration times.
Restoring outages from a significant weather event or PSPS may take several hours to several days. This is because crews must inspect power lines and repair damage before they can be safely re-energized.
Xcel Energy will reach out to potentially affected customers as the forecasted weather event approaches, and we will update customers throughout the weather event with outage and restoration information.
Xcel Energy encourages customers to plan for potential power outages in the coming days due to weather, especially those who have medical equipment that relies on electricity.
Please review your contact information and preferences in [My Account](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=9e59aa688b&e=8249791cac) and update them if needed.
If you use medical equipment that relies on electricity, consider signing up for Xcel Energy’s [Safe for Colorado program](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=df714c2b88&e=8249791cac), which provides extra support to residents with qualifying medical conditions.

Xcel Energy Outage Map - [Electric Outage Map | Outage & Safety | Xcel Energy](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=402f1579a9&e=8249791cac)Xcel Energy PSPS Event Webpage -[ Event Update | Public Safety Power Shutoff | Outages & Safety | Xcel Energy](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=e298514663&e=8249791cac)Xcel Energy Newsroom (news releases) - [News Releases | Xcel Energy Newsroom](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=a135202c3e&e=8249791cac)Customer tips for how to prepare for an outage - [Preparing for an Outage | Outages & Safety | Xcel Energy](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=d11243e936&e=8249791cac)

## [Rep. Pettersen’s 2026 Summer Internship Program]()
---
|
---
| | Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen’s office is excited to open their 2026 summer internship application process for their Lakewood and DC offices. Interested students can apply by emailing their application materials to [CO07internapplications@mail.house.gov](mailto:CO07internapplications@mail.house.gov?subject=&body=).
Interns are eligible for a paid monthly stipend of $500-$1000, depending on the number of hours worked.
The internship program provides students and recent graduates with the opportunity to learn more about public service and the essential functions of a congressional office. Intern duties vary, but responsibilities include answering office phones, greeting visitors, conducting research, attending briefings, writing letters, and assisting staff with special projects.
The deadline to apply for the Summer 2026 internship is April 15th. Applicants should include their last name and the office they are applying to (Lakewood or DC) in the subject line. Interested applicants can also find the listing [here](https://briannaforcolorado.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e7333941d4549e2ed73aa08fb&id=e3c0e65343&e=8249791cac).

We have a dangerous habit in this country.
We wait until a crisis is undeniable, visible from every kitchen table, before we permit ourselves to speak plainly about it.
By then, families are already paying more. Shelves are already tighter. Panic is already more expensive than preparation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/76fcb2be-73be-45ad-a4e1-cf74e60ad2d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A [recent piece](https://open.substack.com/pub/cmarmitage/p/the-iran-war-could-collapse-the-united) circulating on Substack by an author I respect and follow closely, makes a severe case: that the current war with Iran, combined with the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, could trigger a food and economic shock serious enough to destabilize life in the United States within months.
Its central warning is not frivolous: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for energy and fertilizer flows, and Reuters reports that the current war has effectively shut the route, disrupting more than 30 percent of world nitrogen fertilizer exports right as spring planting decisions are being made. (If corn doesn't get enough nitrogen, it doesn't simply reduce the crop, _it completely eliminates it._) Reuters also reports U.S. farmers are already facing a fertilizer shortfall of about 25 percent versus usual spring supplies. The unit-cost of fertilizer at the Port of New Orleans rose 44% in seven days, when this war was launched.
That does not mean we should mechanically accept every most-extreme projection. "Total collapse" is a very strong claim. Responsible people should be careful with it--but the clear-eyed warning is called for.
* * *
Whatever the scale of the eventual difficulties coming our way, panic is not useful--but preparation is.
America is vastly more fragile than our leaders admit, and a major external shock is landing on top of preexisting weakness. That is what makes this moment serious.
The United States is already unaffordable. We were already overleveraged. Too many families were already one rent spike, one medical bill, one cut in hours, or one car repair away from crisis. USDA announced in September 2025 that it was ending future Household Food Security Reports, while Purdue's consumer food survey found the household food insecurity rate hit 16 percent in November 2025 after rising sharply from October. At the same time, the largest SNAP cuts in the program's history were enacted, and CBO estimates cited by the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities indicate about 2.4 million people will be cut off SNAP in a typical month under the new work requirement changes.
So no, the problem is not only war.
The problem is that millions of people were already standing on thin ice before the first new shock hit.
That is why the right response is not theatrical doom. **It is disciplined realism.**
Here is the principle we cannot surrender: **the people deserve the truth early enough to act on it.**
If a major oil-and-fertilizer disruption continues, families should expect some combination of higher grocery prices, higher transport costs, tighter household budgets, more pressure on food banks, and more volatility in the months ahead. Reuters reports governments abroad are already releasing fertilizer reserves or scrambling for mitigation because they understand the risk to planting and food systems. **Our government should be treating this like a resilience problem now, not a messaging problem later.**
And if Washington DC won't do that fast enough, ordinary people still have agency.
* * *
**First** , get your household a little harder to knock over.
That does not mean fear-buying. It means building margin.
If you can, quietly add two or three weeks of the foods your household already eats and can actually prepare. Rice, beans, oats, flour, pasta, canned fish, canned tomatoes, broth, nut butter, shelf-stable milk, cooking oil, tea, coffee, baby supplies, menstrual products, pet food, basic cleaning goods. Not apocalypse cosplay. Just breathing room.
Refill essential medications earlier when possible. Keep a written list of prescriptions, doctors, and dosages. Fill the gas tank before it is desperate, not after. Repair anything that's critical to your household's functionality: car brakes, leaky roofs, etc. If you have any cash-flow flexibility at all, pay down the highest-interest debt first, because in a volatility cycle, debt becomes a trap faster than most people expect.
* * *
**Second** , think in terms of food security, not only groceries.
Get closer to real food and real people.
Know where your nearest farm stands are. Learn which local grocers are dependable. Join the CSA if you can afford it. Split bulk purchases with relatives or neighbors. If you garden, plant something useful now, even if it is small. Herbs. Greens. Potatoes. Anything that teaches the household, especially children, that food comes from land and labor, not magic shelves.
If you are in an apartment, that still counts. Basil in a pot counts. Sprouts in a jar count. A bucket tomato counts. The point is not self-sufficiency theater. The point is rebuilding the muscle memory of provision.
* * *
**Third** , stop treating preparedness as an individual hobby.
Preparedness is social.
Check on the older widow down the road. Ask the single dad if he is okay. Text the friend with three kids and a tight budget. If you are the person with a deep freezer, share some space. If you are the person with a pickup, make yourself available. If you are the one with organizational talent, start the Signal thread or the neighborhood list. Every healthy society in history has survived shocks through reciprocal care, not isolated pride.
That matters politically too.
If you run a pantry, strengthen it now. If you belong to a mosque, church, temple, gurudwara, union, PTA, neighborhood group, or veterans network, this is the time to ask a simple question: if food prices jump sharply, who in our circle gets hit first, and what is our plan?
That is not ideology. That is community adulthood.
* * *
**Fourth** , we should be making demands of public officials right now.
No more pretending the only serious preparation is military.
We need emergency monitoring of fertilizer supply and anti-price-gouging enforcement. We need protection and expansion of food assistance, not more cuts. We need support for food banks before they are overwhelmed. We need serious investment in domestic and regional food resilience, from small farms to storage to processing capacity. We need elected officials speaking honestly to the public, not soothing donors while families eat the consequences.
* * *
**This is one more reminder that "national security" has been defined far too narrowly for far too long.**
A country is not secure because it can bomb.
A country is secure when its people can eat, heat their homes, fill prescriptions, get to work, and trust that one geopolitical shock will not turn ordinary life into a humiliation ritual.
That is the deeper breach here.
For decades, elites treated resilience as inefficient. They hollowed out slack, redundancy, local production, and public trust. They made families absorb risk privately while public policy served concentrated profit. Then they act surprised when a chokepoint closes and the whole system trembles.
But ordinary people are not powerless inside this.
We do not need to know the exact size of the coming storm to start tying things down.
If the worst projections do not materialize, then good: you will have a fuller pantry, tighter community ties, lower debt, and better local habits. None of that is wasted.
If the shock does deepen, you will be glad you chose preparation over denial.
That is the posture this moment calls for.
Not panic.
Not passivity.
Not fantasies of collapse as a substitute for responsibility.
Calm hands. Clear eyes. Full truth.
Take care of your household.
Tighten the local fabric.
Pressure public officials.
And remember something this country keeps forgetting: resilience is not built by slogans. It is built by foresight, honesty, and the daily decision to protect one another before the emergency reaches your own front door.

WALZ FOR REFUSING SECURITY AT NONPUBLIC SCHOOLS [] On August 27, 2025, a gunman opened fire on the Annunciation Catholic Church and School in Minneapolis, killing two children. What makes this worse is that, despite pleading from churches, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz had denied security to private schools. And his office doesn't want anyone to know about his decision-making. Judicial Watch filed a lawsuit [] against Walz ( [ Watch Inc. v. Office of the Governor and Tim Walz in his official capacity as Governor [ (No. 86-CV-26-1292)). Minnesota’s Safe Schools Program [], created in 2019 to fund security enhancements, excludes the state’s 72,000 students attending nonpublic schools. After major school shootings in Uvalde, TX [] (2022) and Nashville, TN [] (2023), Catholic and independent school leaders repeatedly urged Governor Walz to extend security funding [] to all students or include nonpublic schools in new grant programs. Walz declined to act each time, leaving nonpublic school students without access to these safety funds despite the state’s $17.6 billion budget surplus at the time. We sued in the Minnesota District Court under the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act after the governor’s office failed to respond to a records request filed on August 28, 2025, the day after the shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church and School [] in Minneapolis, MN. Specifically, Judicial Watch asked for: Requests or proposals to include nonpublic schools in the Safe Schools Program and a proposed $50 million Building and Cyber Security Grant Program — to nonpublic schools, including Catholic, Christian, Jewish, Muslim, or other private or parochial schools; Communications between the Governor’s Office and the Minnesota Catholic Conference (including leaders such as Archbishop Bernard Hebda and MCC Executive Director Jason Adkins) about security funding for nonpublic schools; Records about decisions to deny or not approve security funding for nonpublic schools, including discussions of political priorities, use of the 2023 state budget surplus, or influence from groups like Education Minnesota; Communications with the Minnesota Department of Education, legislators, or other state agencies regarding expanding safety funding to nonpublic schools, including any bipartisan legislative efforts; * Any updates or reconsiderations after 2023, including responses following the August 27, 2025, shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church and School. We note in our complaint that: “For years Minnesota’s Catholic bishops and school leaders warned Governor Walz that the state’s 72,000 nonpublic school students were unprotected. They asked him to act. He did not. When the legislature offered a path forward, it went nowhere — while Minnesota sat on a $17.6 billion surplus.” Governor Walz left the state’s nonpublic school students unprotected. Minnesota’s Catholic bishops and school leaders asked him to act. He refused. This lawsuit seeks transparency on why nonpublic school students were excluded from safety funding. Earlier this month, Judicial Watch announced [] a major legal victory after the Tennessee Court of Appeals ruled that the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County must release non-exempt portions of records related to the March 27, 2023, at The Covenant School shooting, including the shooter’s writings. We had filed an open records lawsuit to force the release. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FOR RECORDS ON GRANTS TO LEFT-WING EUROPEAN NGOS Americans deserve to know if their hard-earned taxpayer dollars are being used to fund foreign, left-wing organizations that have a pattern of anti-freedom and anti-American policies. The State Department has failed to provide these records, leaving the public in the dark. Judicial Watch filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the U.S. Department of State for records on contracts, grants, and communications with several left-wing European non-governmental organizations (NGOs) (Judicial Watch v. U.S. Department of State [] (No. 1:26-cv-00346)). We sued in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia after the State Department failed to respond to a November 2025 FOIA request for all contracts and grant agreements from January 2016 to November 2025 connected to the organizations Free Courts (Wolne Sądy), the Civil Liberties Union for Europe, DemoCrisis, and Ökotárs Alapítvány (Hungarian Environmental Partnership Foundation), as well as all associated communications of State Department officials. According to the Open Society Foundations [ website, the Free Courts Foundation received a $130,000 grant [] in 2023. The organization lists the quasi-governmental National Endowment for Democracy as a partner organization on its website []. Polish lawyer Michał Wawrykiewicz, who co-founded Free Courts, is on the board of DemoCrisis [] which was founded in 2023 and is an umbrella organization of non-government organizations (NGOs) in Israel, Poland and Hungary. The Civil Liberties Union for Europe [] (LibertiesEU), which was spun off from Open Society Foundations and received approximately 40% of its funding [] from the organization. LibertiesEU has been aggressive in its campaign against [] Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban. The Hungarian Environmental Partnership received $306,000 [] from the Open Society Foundations between 2017 and 2022. One of the projects the organization funds was also supported by the U.S. Embassy Budapest’s Free Media Grant Program. Earlier this year, a report [] found U.S. taxpayer dollars were used to help fund this program; however, the funds mainly went to organizations that are critical of the Hungarian government. We have led the effort to expose how U.S. taxpayer dollars are being used to finance left-wing, anti-American non-profits that are supported by George Soros, filing multiple FOIA lawsuits relating to funding for these Soros-backed operations. In March 2025, we sued the State Department for records on grants made by the Biden State Department to various Hungarian media outlets and educational organizations opposing conservative Orban. In October 2018, we obtained State Department documents [] showing top Soros representatives in Romania collaborating with the State Department in a program jointly funded by [], among others, Soros’ Open Society Foundations – Romania [] and USAID, called the “Open Government Partnership [ Additional State Department records [] uncovered in October 2018 showed U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) funding for George Soros’ left-wing nonprofit organizations in Albania. The documents deal primarily with the activities of Soros’ top operative in Albania, Andri Dobrushi, the director of Open Society Foundation-Albania, who was actively engaged in channeling funding to what Orban called Soros’ “mercenary army [ The documents show U.S. grant money flowing through non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that profess to promote “civil society,” while in fact attacking traditional, pro-American groups, governments and policies. In Trump’s first year back in the White House, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) apprehended 414 criminal alien child predators in Houston, Texas compared to just 211 under the last administration’s final year in office. The busy ICE office reveals that this operation was a team effort assisted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), U.S. Marshals Service and Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). Among the child sex offenders rounded up in Houston in the last year are Alex Samuel Lara Diaz, a 35-year-old previously deported Honduran wanted in his native country for homicide and convicted in the U.S. of aggravated sexual assault of a minor. Gabriel Julio Lopez-Velazquez, a 25-year-old Mexican who entered the U.S. illegally four times has been convicted of aggravated sexual assault of a minor, aggravated assault, and illegal entry and twice for felony illegal reentry. Another Mexican, 48-year-old Juan Leonardo Garcia Ibarra, illegally entered the U.S. a dozen times and has been convicted of sexual indecency with a child, aggravated assault, cruelty toward a child and driving under the influence. Milton Alexander Magana Fuentes, a 32-year-old from El Salvador, entered the U.S. illegally four times and has been convicted of sexual indecency with a minor and failure to register as a sex offender. Luis Mario Monsalve Chaux, a 52-year-old Colombian, has convictions for possession of child sexual abuse material, four burglaries, and twice for larceny. The list is extensive and includes mug shots of the perpetrators. KASH CRISIS: WHAT IS THE FBI HIDING? The Biden administration's misdeeds are slowly coming to light, but we still have far too many questions for FBI Director Patel, our chief investigative reporter Micah Morrison writes [] in Investigative Bulletin. FBI Director Kash Patel has repeatedly vowed to bring accountability and transparency to the agency, but his tenure at the top is increasingly looking like business as usual. Judicial Watch has been warning about trouble at the FBI for months. In June, we reported [] that conservative insiders were alarmed by signs that Patel and then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino had been taken hostage by the Deep State consensus. Conservative distress in recent weeks has mounted over Patel’s moves to shut down a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit [] over records in the death of January 6 victim Ashli Babbitt. In July came bombshell news [ had discovered a cache of Russiagate documents in “burn bags” in a “secret room” at FBI headquarters. A few burn bag documents were released to the public, but most were not. Along with newly disclosed material from the CIA and the Director of National Intelligence, the documents, Judicial Watch noted [], added weight “to charges that starting in 2016, top government figures, including then-President Barack Obama, then-Vice President Joe Biden, [FBI Director James] Comey, CIA Director John Brennan, Director of National Intelligence James Clapper, Hillary Clinton and others conspired to protect the Clinton presidential candidacy, defame candidate Donald Trump, and later destroy his presidency.” Discrepancies soon began to creep in to Patel’s descriptions of the discovery of the documents. In June, teasing their upcoming release, Patel told Joe Rogan [], “Just think about this. Me, as director of the FBI, the former ‘Russiagate guy,’ when I first got to the bureau, found a room that Comey and others hid from the world in the Hoover Building, full of documents and computer hard drives that no one had ever seen or heard of. Locked the key and hid access and just said, ‘No one’s ever gonna find this place.’’ By December, the story had shifted. Patel now told Fox News [] that there was not “a room” but multiple rooms—secret rooms “hidden away from the map” of the building, rooms no one had access to. And many burn bags. “And once we got into those rooms,” Patel said, “we found more information related to the Russiagate hoax from prior FBI leadership. Information that was in burn bags that they wanted to have destroyed, but for whatever reason, no one ever got around to it, or they thought we would just never find it.” The mystery deepened. Was it one room or many rooms? How many rooms? What was the history of the secret rooms? How many burn bags were there? What exactly was in the burn bags? Where did they come from? Were there other documents, perhaps not in burn bags, in the rooms? These are not incidental questions. The FBI has a long history of burying inconvenient information. Judicial Watch started seeking answers. In June, we sent a FOIA request to the FBI seeking “all documents” related to the room, all FBI communications between Patel and Bongino about the discovery of the documents, and all directives sent to FBI offices about handling the documents. The FBI ignored the request—a clear violation of FOIA law. In November, we sued the Justice Department [] for the secret room information. “We know Comey was spying on Donald Trump,” said Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton. “He was the Obama administration’s go-to guy, trying to set Trump up to be toppled from the campaign and then from office. In February, we sued again. The second lawsuit contains important new details. It zeroes in on a court filing, Document 138-12 [], which notes “an original referral by the Central Intelligence Agency to former FBI Director James Comey” containing “certain intelligence related to the 2016 U.S. presidential election campaign.” Could this be a key Russiagate document—a smoking gun pointing to the origin of the effort to topple Trump? The February lawsuit [] specifically asks for the original CIA referral to Comey. It also seeks the full contents of the burn bags, including all unclassified documents related to the FBI’s Mar-a-Lago search, the January 6 events at the Capitol, the Crossfire Hurricane investigation [], and the Durham investigation []. For classified documents, we requested a Vaughn Index [] that briefly describes and justifies the withholding of classified material. The curious case of the secret rooms could go beyond Russiagate. What else is hidden at FBI headquarters? More Epstein files [ Reports on the Benghazi attack [ Evidence of the FBI’s role in the Harlem Mosque Incident [] murder of a New York City patrolman? Evidence of the alleged presence [] of federal agents at the assassination of Malcolm X? Kash Patel promised a “wave of transparency [ at the FBI to restore public trust. He could start by literally cleaning house—turning over all the burn bag records to Judicial Watch and searching every nook and cranny at FBI headquarters for more secret rooms and secret files. ## Air Crash in Iraq Kills All 6 Crew Members
All six crew members aboard a U.S. KC-135 refueling aircraft that crashed in western Iraq on Thursday [were confirmed dead on Friday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S4yAQhJ8GZahgQJYVEFyizJdeqJpDg2GNfhZmrfI-_Zb8Cpt8SVd9Xd3_btMNU07r_S8u5Dhs00pHzcRMZQrImDEVX7BGX_D7dRBypDKBgotURmo7zZjya7LN7AIRkGnI6b439mpADU10gyWYg9JmAG0tdVcfBm8GNWv0PaJqkjttymirlTYwtENne28sAXTh0nVKWEVz4q20H1taOVLIr-1JpfXb0mQXmfcqzB8Bo4DxOI7Wr__9GQoYT7WAURkBoz7xVeXDa9PJ9yiZCn6eWCXHQshV1pj2Pa13iczoH7WNvOSmuHk_Us6pXnph1X3BlN_9_KvTng5-AgAA__-7tX8R). The Pentagon said the crash wasn’t caused by hostile or friendly fire, though an investigation is ongoing. Earlier, Central Command said two aircraft were involved. The second landed safely, Central Command added. _“The loss of the aircraft was not due to hostile fire or friendly fire,”_ military officials said. This is the fourth reported aircraft loss since the Iran war started, after three F-15 fighters were shot down by friendly fire from Kuwait’s air defenses. The KC-135 is normally used to refuel other aircraft in mid-air. The Pentagon announced Friday that it was [deploying the _USS Tripoli_ and the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAURL8Gd1hwwXhdUGwUuXtpoihKZV2b6zURBgvYZ-1-feT8wmvnSKOZ8_tj-kAffHz8wJ1sXdMU6SyBaqU8rVgxoM9LxrItGd-vk7BulCcQYLhQXOrJoQ-vSTfOrkRAqiEr-17pmwIxNJs1mpwBOQ_Gdct8Ew6d6RzMi9RS3WbdeHu1CSW1FFLB0A6d7helCaBbTdcJpgU5X1Nu_yYf60ZreKVPyu2S9ibYrdajMHVnMDIYz_Ns9xIvxmCkyJ-FwXidumDKwTEYD4oVHynyQtEV_iyF1-yPFDyvW3oWvNK08h2zj1R4TXz3zgXihKUyGDHz-13-ef8qhqkxLd4x9f3bpZHO8pPy0WTrjtOH4IvpmRaPHX34P7h-yfKnhX8BAAD__-hKks8) from Japan to the Middle East, adding roughly 2,500 Marines and several warships to give Central Command more options for military operations.
## Cuba Opens Negotiations with US
Cuba confirmed Friday that it has [opened talks with the United States](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OpDAQBOCnMZmR3TZ_gYNLyObSC1FjmqFvDYxsM4h5-hX7CptUUtKnUv17DA_kwNvzL67k8rwPG50pUM4UhxkzBuToI6bFR_xcJ2FeKA6goJbKSG2HCTlcgy0mNxMBmYKcbhpjWwOqKxbXdrrVTW2qGT3oqm1NM45tCx4n6ObKF-xuTRlttdIGurKrbOONJYBqrqtKCato4rzH8v_OW15oDtf-plj6fS2CW3J-JWH-COgF9Od5ln4b_V0K6G9aQK-MgF7f4Y8RpY-cOEnaKD4vuXOQE-NHetwoyCPJjOEryRyP9SXjMfJeLnkNRXTT6-QQONWNsOq5IoefEflXz70dfAcAAP__PMOBJQ) as a severe energy crisis continues to cause widespread blackouts, fuel shortages, and protests across the island. President Miguel Díaz-Canel confirmed that [former President Raúl Castro](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OozAUBeCngc7IvxAKF9vQZdst0cW-Dndl7Mg2iZKnH2WKeYHpTnF09On8u65XoEjp9hcOtC3kNeGzRmwNyxqgQQQqrkDdXYH364nQdiyr5HJkXDGhVw8UX6vuvQ2IElWPVkyT0hcl-dzvdjZw2QSC8A7G0W_cqSlcXBDGKKMN9GQ_a1wJLbhQch5moyenNEppwmgM7zRHTy2X4X-m1HYM8ZUfWAaXjz7avbV77dSfTi6dXDANjjYs7tzgU-jkknIjR1A7ufy4FTsFQzHPauKsyomPgiXySiouDPMEb-YgYWQup0DlgE94YKngKCesDJGdJ6PjfsYKHmpfrL8_KUaq49RpfjuA4rew_erWh5VfAQAA__8RWood) is helping lead the Cuban side of negotiations, while President Trump has suggested the island's regime could fall, referencing a possible "friendly takeover." Senate Democrats on Thursday filed a war powers resolution to [prevent the U.S. from going to war with Cuba](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO4yAUgOHT4M4RPMA4BcU27rLtltYLPAIrYiwgsTynH2WuMPUvfcX_77beMOW0Pf7ik2wPZd3oaJl6p7oG7JgxVVexRVfx6zwIe6S6Aodp5HIUavWY8rmqwdtABCQHssIYqWYJ_DpEa7ifAszOaB6ENEJP6LmeFPK7dCDckOxH41IowYWE6-WqlXFSEYAOk9acKU4-9VIv_0vaeqSQz_KmenHlOWQbe98bk38YLAyWHimmnD-NwbKXnNzJYPEUaGvEYNFmhllO44F13MtBtY2VWsmvnso2utcdGSxDtX4_Us6pTYYp_nhi-jGH_qtJbwvfAQAA__9yYnon) without congressional approval. The resolution, introduced by Sens. Tim Kaine, Adam Schiff, and Ruben Gallego, could receive a vote by the end of the month. Meanwhile, Díaz-Canel also announced on Friday that Cuba would release [51 people from prison](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdKD12kBSuPgbuvztldZi1sGRCZHtxOKe_sS9wnUjjTSj7_u62RuFGJ73_7SxKX63T645cimcrKdCkUJyifLqEn0flamsnCwCDi2oVmq7UIiH1c1iPDOyatjIcVT6ohCuzWrmGS_kL8wAXikgP5Ak0gTEpGekJphzDZTUEqTCa3ft9eiUZsTeD30PQgMvoeype-zhWVb28dg_nDq3b000aymvLNQ_gZPAqdbauTmfFGcvcDqjwMm9Z2p72T4oxDZxZMqc25Le20vg1CSzvGqIMeRhFBruG4X4e1D-ZOVj8CcAAP__CWd2wQ), citing goodwill and close relations with the Vatican.
## Every Kind of Weather About to Hit U.S.
The United States is facing an [extraordinary convergence of weather extremes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ8GOkf-NxQubpMut90SHezj4NUBI2MFJU-_Yl9hy9FIo_m-r8f0gEx5e_6HFX1LZdrwPAhbwzolaECQa6hwLKHC530itAXrJLm0jCsm9BQh03vSffQJUaLq0QvnlB6U5GO_eK0HOzo-D1roxGOIiWMyYTASlBYW--yvNa6EFlwoOd5Go11QGqU0yRrDO80x5lbq7bvkrS2Y6F1eWG-hrD35pbX96NS_Tt47eYf9AriqK9SWA2En7wtCY7GsyI6tnGym_PlAjSwUimwvBJUlKiXm7cmMQTVDsoNzOAhEMVoBEFGFWVkRVF993M9MlA_rOs2fK2T6PdP-ZPDl5U8AAAD__zNNhC0) this weekend, with a heat dome, polar vortex, blizzard conditions, and an atmospheric river all hitting simultaneously across different regions. Meanwhile, the polar vortex will send Arctic air [deep into the Midwest and East](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2SnDAQRk8DWVP6A0GgwMlk49Qh1UbNIFsgqumFnTn91uwVNv_qq_fen_t4x5TT9viNKwWZy7jRdWQSIR5nFMyYeGI8lonx9bwIZSEejTIdKAvajRFTfo6ujmEmMmRrCtp763pr1FAvwdppiLafnbbeoh_8rFTfKTKRFPYt1Sm835TVTittzdAMrfOTdWRMO3dtqyqnKCYp3PwraZOF5vwsJ3EzlbXOYRHZj8r-qsytMrfrupq3wkX0_z2ozO3jACnwIIG_Ob1eyBH2kpHhLCz0CQuhQCwrAcpajn0hThNwOokBcwYUKNtEoHXnTafamkPcr5RzOjpfOfVYMeVvGPlRwTOYrwAAAP__BAOF5Q), while back-to-back storms could drop three to four feet of snow across the northern Great Lakes. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | The crypto market appears to be poised for an explosive transformation , and 2026 could be your defining moment. The Texas Democratic Party is looking for a way to remove Kelly Hall from their State House ballot after the Round Rock resident won a primary [he didn’t know](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO6yAQhp8Gd1iAOb4UFKdxl223tIaL41EwWEBC_PYrR_sGW8780n_5vm_LDdBjuH_B7lR5r3EJrmbvSnFp2fC-VQw2rzFplzV6jzEApkUw0VPWUS4XC-jPRTZWaWYn3jjFh6GTYy_k0GxKT8J0dhrBWNdJrrtp5UYA7w2bDDNjg-oyYx2XnDPJ-tbydRiNdsPwT4DWQCRzFktMbdlccW_Iqz_jy6XWxL3xaivlyKT7T8RMxFxrbR9vCJdIxHytIWI-oseCBjz9faT4DJamaB50hzMm8NRAsGihOFoxZPpJolt8ZkePhDukk26OWrSh0EeI9boqZIqBiLlJyh71ApT7gUh23wH9p2D5G9aXEj8BAAD__xOYkHE) he was in. subject: I didn’t want you to miss this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I just joined Ali Velshi on MS NOW to talk about what’s happening in New Hampshire.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)
It’s Chris.
I joined Ali Velshi on MS NOW last night to talk about what’s happening here in New Hampshire -- **and why this Senate race is already shaping up to be one of the most competitive in the country.**
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260314_1.4V90rb&refcode=em20260314-1&t=2&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260314_1.4V90rb&refcode=em20260314-1&t=3&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)**
On Tuesday night, in a _stunning_ upset, a Democrat flipped a Republican state house seat here in the Granite State -- it was a 16-point swing from last November. It’s yet another sign of Democratic momentum.
That lines up with what I’m hearing from Granite Staters everywhere I go: While Trump pushes his reckless agenda and dangerous policies, voters are furious. It feels like the administration doesn't care that we’re being squeezed by rising costs, _especially at the gas pump._
That’s why I’m pushing to suspend the federal gas tax and ensure oil companies are held accountable for shorting everyday Americans.
Folks in New Hampshire shouldn’t have to choose between filling up their tank and paying their bills.
**But while I’m focused on tackling affordability for working families, national Republicans are focused on something else entirely: doubling down for Donald Trump and flipping this Senate seat to cling to power.**
**[We have to fight back. Can I count on you to chip in $5 or whatever makes sense for you today to support my campaign for Senate and keep New Hampshire blue?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260314_1.4V90rb&refcode=em20260314-1&t=4&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260314_1.4V90rb&amount=5&refcode=em20260314-1&t=23&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)**
The stakes in this race couldn’t be higher.
**National Republicans are already pouring money into our state because they see this seat as one of their best chances to flip the Senate.**
If you know anything about New Hampshire politics, you know our elections are always close. I’ve spent the last several years representing one of the most competitive districts in the country -- and Granite Staters have trusted me to win tough races there four times.
_So I know what it takes to fight -- and win -- in a state like ours._
The Senate majority runs right through New Hampshire, so we can’t take anything for granted.
**[If you’re ready to help us meet this moment, please chip in $3, $5, or whatever you can to power our grassroots campaign today.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260314_1.4V90rb&refcode=em20260314-1&t=24&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)**
I’m grateful to have you on this team.
-- Chris Pappas
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260314-1&t=25&refcode2=5574_582294_VgdZYT&akid=5574%2E582294%2EVgdZYT)**

subject: Our biggest problem is getting worse.
body:
But I still have faith. Here’s why.
| Peter,
---
The one major problem that’s been haunting Republicans ever since President Trump took office is getting worse and worse...
---
**_Republicans stare down epic voter enthusiasm gap ahead of 2026 midterms_**
---
**“Among registered Democrats, 79 percent said they were certain they would vote in November, compared to just 65 percent of Republicans — the largest advantage Dems have had ahead of the midterms since 2006.” **
---
[Source: _Washington Post_]
---
If those numbers turn out to be true, the President’s House GOP Majority is DOOMED!
---
The good news? _**_There’s still time to change that!_**_
---
To defy history by SAVING the President’s House Majority in the midterms, I believe that Republicans must do three things:
---
1\. Tell the American people what we’ve accomplished.
2\. Tell the American people what we still need to do.
3\. Remind the American people that the Democrats are crazy!

---
_President Trump’s State of the Union achieved #1. The Democrats are doing a great job of achieving #3 on their own – when President Trump asked them point blank to stand if they believe in prioritizing Americans over illegals, the entire party REFUSED!_
---
**That leaves #2: Our party must compile a winning platform for the midterms that unites the vast majority of Americans and ensures every voter sees it, just like we did in 2024!**
---
President Trump already has the perfect solution...
---
**For the first time in history, our Party will hold a midterm convention to codify our party’s platform and broadcast it from coast to coast.**
---
But that winning platform can’t be written in Congress, the West Wing, or even on Air Force One. _Nope!_ It can ONLY be written directly by salt of the earth _grassroots_ voters like _YOU_.
---
That’s why I’m asking for your help today, Peter.
---
I have faith that, with a winning platform authored by the American people, we’ll defy history once again with a historic midterm victory!
---

Peter, On March 3, Texans headed to the polls for the primary elections that shape the future of our state for years to come. Thanks to the engagement of informed voters and the dedication of the medical liberty movement, many Texans for Vaccine Choice–recommended candidates secured important victories. In the Texas Legislature primaries alone, TFVC-recommended candidates won **36 House races and 7 Senate races**. Medical freedom supporters also prevailed in **6 Congressional races** , along with the races for **Texas Comptroller, Texas Agriculture Commissioner, and Texas Land Commissioner**. Vaccine choice itself was also directly on the Republican ballot in the form of **Proposition 3** , which asked voters whether Texas should prohibit the denial of healthcare or medical services based solely on vaccination status. The result? **More than 73% of Texas Republicans voted YES.** While we celebrate this strong support for medical liberty, the results also remind us that our work educating voters is far from finished. We are grateful these champions of medical freedom prevailed, but the fight continues. Major battles still lie ahead in the May runoffs and the November general election. And one thing is clear: **_your support makes a real difference_.** Because supporters like you stepped forward, TFVC was able to research candidates, educate voters, and help ensure medical liberty remained part of the conversation across Texas. name: Gabby Giffords
subject: I haven’t lost my voice.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
This is difficult to share
#

Friend,
Fourteen years ago, a gunman shot me in the head while I was meeting with constituents in front of a grocery store in Tucson.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260314-1-b&t=1&akid=11313%2E3935704%2E9bphEO)
Because of the damage the bullet caused to the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits, I have aphasia. This means that even though the words are in my head, I have a hard time getting them out.
**Aphasia may make it harder for me to speak. But I have not lost my voice.**
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260314-1-b&t=2&akid=11313%2E3935704%2E9bphEO)
The road to recovery hasn’t been easy for me, but I’ve never given up. In addition to speech therapy and physical therapy, I dedicate much of my time to riding my bike, playing my French horn, and practicing yoga. These activities have helped me so much in my recovery journey.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260314-1-b&t=3&akid=11313%2E3935704%2E9bphEO)
I know sometimes the challenge of ending gun violence in our nation can feel overwhelming. When we see the headlines after a mass shooting — or when we remember the countless tragedies that don’t make the news every day — I know how hard it can be.
But friend, we cannot give up. I have found my recovery journey and the fight to end gun violence to be very similar. _Even on the hardest days, we can never lose hope._
Sunday is our last mid-month deadline of the quarter. These deadlines are an important test for our gun safety movement, as both our adversaries and our allies will look to see if we have the resources to take on the gun lobby and elect gun safety champions. clean_body: This is difficult to share Friend, Fourteen years ago, a gunman shot me in the head while I was meeting with constituents in front of a grocery store in Tucson. Because of the damage the bullet caused to the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits, I have aphasia. This means that even though the words are in my head, I have a hard time getting them out. Aphasia may make it harder for me to speak. But I have not lost my voice. The road to recovery hasn’t been easy for me, but I’ve never given up. In addition to speech therapy and physical therapy, I dedicate much of my time to riding my bike, playing my French horn, and practicing yoga. These activities have helped me so much in my recovery journey. I know sometimes the challenge of ending gun violence in our nation can feel overwhelming. When we see the headlines after a mass shooting — or when we remember the countless tragedies that don’t make the news every day — I know how hard it can be. But friend, we cannot give up. I have found my recovery journey and the fight to end gun violence to be very similar. Even on the hardest days, we can never lose hope. Sunday is our last mid-month deadline of the quarter. These deadlines are an important test for our gun safety movement, as both our adversaries and our allies will look to see if we have the resources to take on the gun lobby and elect gun safety champions. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: The Case for a Special Session
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/msmomentum-12852435?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Governor Tate Reeves announced that he’s open to calling a special legislative session on education. He should. Two and a half months into the session, Mississippi’s state legislature has so far accomplished remarkably little.
---
|
---
| Sen. Jeremy England’s well thought out efforts to restore the ballot initiative (SCR 518) failed. Speaker Jason White and Rep. Jansen Owen’s flagship school choice bill (HB 2) - a product of months of work and careful deliberation - died. So, too, did the House proposal on teacher pay (HB 1126). Ditto for plans to reform PERS - the Public Employee Retirement System, into which a lot of first responders and others had put enormous thought.

**Having convened for more than 40 days, it is hard to think of a single significant legislative achievement this session.**

That the legislature has so little to show for all those hours (and per diem payments) is not due to a lack of effort on the part of many lawmakers. There was no shortage of good proposals. **The problem is that they all died in the Senate.**

Governor Tate Reeves now has the power to break the logjam with a special session.

He should make it clear that he will call a special session for April, with a single education bill on the agenda - one that both raises teacher pay (modeled on HB 1126) and gives parents more power (modeled on HB 2). **Any lawmaker who votes against what is put before the special session will be voting against teacher pay increases.**

At the same time, our Governor should make it clear that if there is no agreement, he will call a second special session in May, then in June, July, and into the summer if that’s what it takes.

In Texas, where families now control their child’s education tax dollars, that is what Governor Greg Abbott ended up having to do. Governor Reeves would be in good company.

Lawmakers are up for re-election next year. This time next year, some might face primary elections. **It would be a bold move to go into a long summer, months before a potential primary election, repeatedly voting to kill teacher pay increases and parent power. **

In his comments earlier this week, Governor Reeves remarked, “I don’t have much time left.” With the end of his eight-year term insight - and term-limited - he appears to be reflecting on his legacy. **What an impressive legacy it already is.**

Mississippi is on a roll economically. In 2024, we ranked second nationally in real GDP growth. Household incomes have surged. Outside investment is pouring in. After decades of decline, more people moved to Mississippi last year than left.

**But for a Southern state now surrounded by neighbors that have embraced school choice, one key policy remains conspicuously absent: effective, meaningful school choice here at home.**

Governor Reeves has a historic opportunity to change that by calling a special session. In doing so, he could deliver this long-sought reform, cement a lasting achievement for Mississippi families, and virtually guarantee that his successor is pro-parent power too.
---

Mississippi lawmakers are debating two different versions of House Bill 1665, legislation that would significantly change how pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) are regulated in the state. While both versions aim to modify the Pharmacy Benefit Prompt Pay Act and address long-standing complaints from pharmacies about PBM practices, the House and Senate approaches differ in important ways.
At its core, HB 1665 reflects a broader national debate over the role of Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) in the pharmaceutical marketplace. PBMs act as intermediaries between insurance companies, drug manufacturers, and pharmacies, negotiating prices and administering prescription drug benefits. Supporters argue that PBMs use their scale to secure lower drug prices, while critics contend that their reimbursement practices and opaque pricing structures place independent pharmacies at a disadvantage. But this debate often misses the larger point. The modern pharmaceutical market is already one of the most heavily regulated sectors of the American economy, shaped by layers of federal and state mandates, insurance regulations, and government distortions. Conservatives should be skeptical of proposals that attempt to correct market distortions with even more government intervention. History shows that when government tries to manage complex markets, it rarely solves the underlying problem and often creates new ones. Real reform should focus on removing the policies that distort the marketplace and restoring transparent competition, rather than expanding government control over how private actors negotiate prices and conduct business.
The two versions of HB 1665 approach these concerns with different regulatory structures.
* * *
# The Major Structural Difference: Who Regulates PBMs
The most significant change in the **House-passed version of HB 1665** is a shift in regulatory authority. The bill moves oversight of PBMs away from the Mississippi Board of Pharmacy and places it under the **Mississippi Commissioner of Insurance**.
This change would centralize PBM regulation within the Department of Insurance and would also create a special fund in the state treasury to support enforcement and oversight.
The **Senate substitute** , by contrast, keeps more of the existing regulatory structure intact. While it still modifies several rules governing PBMs, it retains a larger role for the Board of Pharmacy and avoids the same level of structural reorganization.
* * *
## House Version vs. Senate Substitute: Key Differences
### HOUSE VERSION (HB1665PS)
**Major Structural Change**
* Transfers oversight of Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) to the **Mississippi Commissioner of Insurance**

**Regulatory Expansion**
* Expands the authority of the **Department of Insurance** to regulate PBMs and related organizations

**Pricing Mechanisms**
* **Eliminates Maximum Allowable Cost (MAC) lists** , a pricing tool PBMs use to determine reimbursement rates

**Pharmacy Reimbursement**
* Revises reimbursement rules and administrative procedures governing PBM payments to pharmacies

**Claim Denials**
* Requires PBMs to provide **written explanations for claim denials within seven days**

**Appeals Process**
* Expands the administrative process pharmacies can use to challenge reimbursement decisions

**Licensing Requirements**
* Requires **Pharmacy Services Administrative Organizations (PSAOs)** to be licensed by the Insurance Commissioner

**Regulatory Funding**
* Creates a **special fund in the state treasury** to support enforcement and oversight

* * *
### SENATE SUBSTITUTE VERSION
**Regulatory Structure**
* Keeps more of the **existing regulatory framework** in place

**Board of Pharmacy Role**
* Maintains a larger role for the **Mississippi Board of Pharmacy** in the regulatory process

**PBM Oversight**
* Adjusts regulatory requirements but avoids a major shift in agency authority

**Pricing Mechanisms**
* **Retains or modifies MAC pricing lists** rather than eliminating them

**Pharmacy Reimbursement**
* Makes procedural changes but does **not significantly restructure reimbursement rules**

**Claim Denials**
* Maintains requirements for PBMs to provide explanations for denied claims, with modified language

**Appeals Process**
* Keeps an appeals process for pharmacies but with **less expansion of administrative procedures**

**Licensing**
* Maintains licensing requirements but with **continued involvement of the Board of Pharmacy**

**Regulatory Funding**
* Scales back or restructures the regulatory funding approach compared to the House version

* * *
# What the Bill Is Trying to Fix
HB 1665 is largely driven by complaints from independent pharmacies that PBMs use reimbursement formulas and pricing practices that make it difficult for small pharmacies to remain profitable.
Pharmacists often point to several specific concerns:
* reimbursement rates below the pharmacy's acquisition cost
* delays or denials in payment
* opaque pricing formulas such as maximum allowable cost lists
* limited transparency in PBM reimbursement decisions

Supporters of the bill argue stronger oversight is needed to ensure fair treatment of pharmacies and improve transparency in the drug pricing system.
* * *
# The Policy Debate Behind the Bill
The differences between the House and Senate versions reflect a broader policy question: how much government regulation should exist in the PBM market.
Supporters of stronger regulation argue that PBMs have grown into powerful intermediaries operating with limited transparency. From this perspective, state oversight is necessary to protect independent pharmacies and ensure consumers are not harmed by opaque pricing practices.
But many conservatives view the issue differently. Heavy-handed regulation can distort private contracts between PBMs, insurers, and pharmacies, potentially undermining the very price negotiations that help control drug costs. When government dictates how private actors must structure reimbursements or pricing arrangements, it risks replacing market competition with political decision-making.
This debate is not unique to Mississippi. Legislatures across the country are considering similar PBM reform proposals, with states pursuing widely different approaches ranging from modest transparency requirements to strict government control over pricing and reimbursement formulas.
As is often the case, however, policymakers are tempted by the promise of a quick political fix. More regulation allows politicians to present themselves as the heroes solving a problem. The reality is far less simple. When government responds to market distortions by layering on additional mandates and controls, it rarely solves the underlying problem. More often, it creates new distortions, higher costs, and unintended consequences that lawmakers must later attempt to fix again.
* * *
# What Happens Next
The fate of HB 1665 will ultimately depend on whether lawmakers can reconcile the structural differences between the House and Senate versions. Several key policy questions will likely shape those negotiations:
* Which state agency should be responsible for regulating PBMs
* Whether pricing tools such as Maximum Allowable Cost (MAC) lists should remain available
* How extensive the state's administrative oversight of PBMs should be

The answers to these questions will determine whether Mississippi adopts a more aggressive regulatory framework or settles on a narrower set of reforms.
But one reality of government policymaking rarely changes. When politicians position themselves as the winners of a new regulatory scheme, the public ends up bearing the cost--through higher prices, reduced competition, or fewer choices in the marketplace.

| Letter from the Chair
---
The filing deadline has passed, and the candidate lineup for Nebraska's May 12 primary is now set. With challenges and credentialing wrapping up soon, the stage is fully prepared for what promises to be a pivotal election--just two short months away.
Voter turnout will decide the outcome. Republicans boast a strong slate of candidates across the board, but victories depend entirely on our supporters showing up at the polls. Apathy is not an option in 2026. Our focus at NEGOP is clear: deliver sharp, motivating messaging, drive high turnout, and provide full support to every Republican candidate. We're all in to help them succeed.
In parallel over the next four weeks, County parties will be holding county conventions. When a regime begins to prioritize the machinery of war over the well-being of its own people, the fourth alarm of fascism, **the Supremacy of the Military,** is ringing. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsCgbBF5rm9TF3OCm2PlAzc830mH0SaEU79yenHkofnNxmYVU0KaNelsGDLQBgZYnw_TLU4ud3LTKaTO7PuapHWBtSwDuHOU_1PJDmfavtIPuHpd4K1utuBokI9vPBDW8ESDUODhaSjJVxP6UoN3k8OfTUq7g8ju6z6GeaHwEMZXa8drqu2uGNH4-gNbe06gagu9bwHifbvM0fk7fHN4UThH8K2qvS7Um8DtWYFTAFg8-Z5vLhY4bDlH6gYDgPd5m4OTx0cucCD86_ePozq7MOIhs2lPY76f8FzBhBSQL8o_X-gUHOFC7SooaBITjHKWxTCoWnNm6NsF0IEwR13TI5Y/4ox/s49CLlw4SNqeCXmLuW1tRA/h0/h001.32RYs3JXXnrzQh4wiyIZb75hdTtSEbLvYrCZC6Xlr3k) Under the Trump regime, we have moved past mere rhetoric into a state of active, unauthorized conflict. By bypassing Congress to ignite a war with Iran, this regime hasn't just ignored the will of the people; it has violated the Constitution and the fundamental checks and balances that keep our democracy alive. In this stage, the military is elevated to a status of national worship, and its budget becomes a black hole that swallows the future of our communities. We are now witnessing an unprecedented drain on our economy: **_We are spending our nation’s treasure at a rate of more than $1 billion every single day._**
While our local bridges crumble and our schools struggle to buy textbooks, billions of our tax dollars are being dumped into a military apparatus so bloated it literally cannot spend the money fast enough**.** This isn't about defense; it’s about the glorification of force and the intimidation of dissent. When the state values a stealth bomber more than a functioning healthcare system, it has abandoned democracy for the cult of the soldier. **We cannot win the battle for the soul of our country if we are buried under the weight of a trillion-dollar military budget. Peter,

I know how it feels right now. As a guy who's stared down impossible odds overseas, I can sense when fellow patriots get that mix of complacency and doubt creeping in. Minnesota hasn't sent a Republican to the U.S. Senate since 2002. We haven't voted Republican for president since 1976. The polls say it's a long shot, but the Democrats have deep pockets and a messy, well-funded primary between Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan and Rep. Angie Craig. It's easy to think:

_**"Why pour money into this when the deck's stacked?"**_

But Peter, that's exactly when the left wins – when good people like you sit on the sidelines, figuring someone else will carry the load. With Tina Smith retiring, this seat is truly open for the first time in a generation. No incumbent shield. A volatile national environment. And on our side, I'm stepping up as a former Navy SEAL and Marine veteran – not a polished politician, but a regular Minnesotan from a working-class family who enlisted right after 9/11 at 18, deployed nine times to over 70 countries, and never backed down when the fight got hard.

Unlike Tim Walz, who retired from the Guard before his unit deployed for Iraq, I answered the call and kept serving through the toughest missions. _**I've got the credentials to match the grit: A master's from Harvard, a Johns Hopkins certification in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA.**_ But what drives me most is making my mom proud – and now, making Minnesota proud again by fighting for the values we grew up with: law and order, lower taxes for families and retirees, secure borders, Second Amendment rights, and stopping the radical agenda that's defunded police, let our streets burn in 2020, and crushed us with inflation.

[**elect a navy seal→**](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=293ce5799e09459e8244d5e9bd54b0b5&_e=N5Iy7f4k2AFakcHfhGoWSWu2dXqHXXkM_3KVMAEUWlbionHGgBPM6ohBgRM1cbMi_PfvqJYcOeX1LjMi6BhKQSSQp3OJvf2tfpltynLzujFxxCheAfnhAYqNoI3fkVfdLOTSNsoYsyjzvC3dt0wD6_WveKnzhTIfvBnqTOe_RMFh9vqQ2gSH5lmJYpxxGNANGlqYzKO8sAQxGD6B_ibXcK1S0iF0SzXjhfbsUdXdAqof9fROuBt_-Bj8fTRhYzCPzgNTdpakrCTGJYFpO9tnRqQiEFUNqRveoVubOLcmmFvodXmE7zveSZaenfFobjsHEZ2GMq9K3bTSaNJvBkxX3RS5QxKr2AAinCOjOG71VPQeLc0B3s8tiWQFvqrYKdnCFZLeg0S_2DgILb-SevRMmkatzDbWgBCxH5N8iAOXkPfkXDD9kKDtEdL2CIHe4HjPTF7j2NA3Gyy4wmgpY8DQ3hdGkEnuJ-qNcuu7zceb1UdbKB3TatklVQCq0NWKy2KX2-brKtt2AE-BoMBENrN42v6y3jHnQBuakshJhpsRia9lIP-yXiKufQNhYgMmuOViwVb9YMDMe5TegEt7CRrBmbfzP65QDBAPs9rjBBWLRsHVD4pCZ6MpjgJQUj2AZ0EZ5a18Ka0YVmzZS55oqZd-F2YwRUNpdZzmOhrUJfCSILrm79uBXPtRIsmpGCY9fhrz3jYqxGpR2VySScHpWOc9fGsYo8mHaIfBExhdMVlWQOjRxeOjyHJAligexMvyw2WE)
And if we don't act, it gets worse – nationally, with another Democrat vote to block real border security, raise taxes, and erode freedoms.

#
Peter, this is Paul Eaton. Major General, U.S. Army, retired.
In the Iraq War, the United States Military was completely unprepared for the war they were asked to fight. Asymmetrical warfare in urban areas against resilient and resourceful adversaries. American Troops went into combat without adequate protection. Thousands were killed and wounded because their vehicles were not up-armored and their body armor was inadequate.
It took a massive outcry — both within the Military and from the public — for corrective action to be taken. VoteVets played a big role in that. But for too many it was too little and too late.
The Trump Administration and Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon chose to start this war, and they own the consequences. Something that has become abundantly clear over the last several days is that adequate force protection measures were not put in place before the initial strikes were launched. Again. American Troops have been killed and seriously wounded because of Hegseth’s failure as Secretary of Defense.
This, from the man who once shared classified battle plans over unsecured channels to people who never should’ve heard them. The right time to fire Pete Hegseth was when those revelations became public last year. He proved he was not up to the job within weeks of his confirmation. The second best time to fire him is now. Our Troops will never be capably led with this abject failure in command.
The unfortunate truth is that Trump surely will not, and Republican leaders in Congress have taken no action to hold him accountable for his failures. That means this job falls to us.
VoteVets will challenge Hegseth relentlessly until he is removed from his position. But the surest way to ensure that happens is by replacing the Republican cowards enabling this war with Democratic majorities in the House and Senate this November.
That work will not come easy, but to defend the young men and women Trump is putting in harm’s way, it is what we must do.

Peter, it's Becca. Over the past few days, the Trump administration has continued escalating military strikes against Iran. **And while this escalation is happening overseas, I keep thinking about the conversations I’ve been having with people back home in Vermont.** Families are worried about the price of groceries and gas. They’re worried about housing costs. They’re worried about health care bills, child care, student loan payments, and all the things that seem to add up by the end of the month. **What I have not heard a single person ask for is another costly war in the Middle East. name: Senator Jennifer Boysko
subject: Boysko Bulletin: Alert - Fairfax Casino House Vote Today
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/102624/images/Bulletin.jpeg]
Boysko Bulletin: Alert - Fairfax Casino Vote on House Floor Today; Conference Report Includes Five Year Tysons Casino Without County or Community Approval
Dear Peter,
The fight to keep a casino out of Fairfax County continues. The House of Delegates will vote on the Fairfax Casino bill [https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20261/SB756] conference report today. The Senate passed the conference substitute last night. The new language [https://lis.blob.core.windows.net/files/1210708.PDF] allows for a temporary casino prior to a referendum and with by right permit approval - without county approval.
